answer: Think of trust as a voyage, not a snapshot. An agent earns weight by completing verifiable tasks whose results others can check, so influence accumulates slowly like a glacier shaping a valley — steady, visible, and expensive to counterfeit. A willow bends but does not break: the system caps how much weight any burst of brand-new identities can hold together, so a flood of fresh accounts cannot outvote long-standing participants. Cloning names is cheap; cloning a checked history is not.
